transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, hi. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time... 

It's just, well, I've been under a little bit of stress lately, and I want to make sure I'm handling it the right way. I don't want to sound like I'm complaining or causing trouble, because I really try to get along with everyone. But... well, for months now, I’ve been trying to get people to understand that my husband’s family is sort of quietly messing with our money and our good name. 

I know how that sounds, I really do, and I hate to even speak badly of them. But I do posting and billing for a living, so I pay attention to details. I'll see these little billing errors show up at work, or... or someone at our church will suddenly act kind of funny or cold toward me for no reason. And no matter what records anyone pulls up to try and explain it away, I just know it ties back to his family. 

I hope that doesn't sound terrible of me to say. Am I explaining that okay? I just want to figure out how to handle it properly.
Do you think it’s possible that you might be mistaken about your husband’s family causing these problems?

Oh, I really wish I was mistaken. I honestly do. I know how it sounds, and I don't want to be difficult or seem stubborn. I always try to look at things logically, you know? I'm not the type to jump to conclusions... 

But... well, when I see those little billing errors pop up at work, and then the very next day someone at church is just... avoiding my eye or acting funny... it's just too much to be a coincidence. I know people pull up records and try to show me, 'Look, it's just a typo,' or 'They were just having a bad day.' And I always smile and say okay, because I really don't want to cause a fuss or make anyone uncomfortable. But deep down, no matter what they show me, I just know it ties back to his family. 

I hope you don't think I'm being completely unreasonable... I'm really trying to look at it fairly, does that make sense?
Have you ever been able to fully convince yourself that your husband’s family is not causing these problems?

I've tried, I really have. I'll sit down and tell myself, 'You're just overthinking this, they wouldn't do that.' And I'll try to just brush it off when the numbers don't add up at work, or when someone at church gives me that... that look. I'll tell myself it's nothing, because I really, really don't want to think badly of them. I want us all to get along.

But then... I'll just be sitting there, and I'll think about the billing errors, and how it all connects, and... I just can't shake it. No matter how hard I try to convince myself otherwise, or what papers people show me, I just know they're behind it. They're quietly messing with our money and our reputation. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds like I'm not trying hard enough to let it go. Am I making any sense at all? I just want to be honest with you about how I'm feeling.
How certain are you that your husband’s family is causing this—could there be any other explanation at all?

I'm one hundred percent certain, doctor. I mean... I wish I wasn't. I really, really wish there was another explanation. It would be so much easier if it was just a mistake, or if I was just... you know, being silly. 

But I've looked at it from every angle, because I really didn't want to accuse them of anything. I don't like conflict. But when you see the billing errors at work, and then you see how people at church are suddenly acting... it all just points back to them. They're quietly messing with our money and our good name, and I just know it in my heart. 

I know it probably sounds awful of me to be so sure about something so terrible. I hope you don't think I'm a bad person for saying it... I'm just trying to be completely honest with you. Is that okay?
Have you ever heard voices that other people could not hear?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that. I... I know sometimes people can go through things where they hear things, and I certainly wouldn't judge anyone who does, but... no, my mind is very quiet that way. 

It's really just my own regular thoughts in there, you know? Just thinking about my work or what to make for dinner, or worrying about the things I mentioned. I've never heard any voices or anything strange like that. I hope that's a good thing to hear... I really am just a very normal person, aside from all this awful stress with his family. 

I'm doing okay answering your questions, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you find yourself avoiding other people because you worry they will criticize, reject, or judge you?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I avoid people. I mean, I still go to work every day, and I still go to church... I try to be friendly with everyone. I've always been a bit of a people pleaser, actually. I like it when everyone gets along. 

I guess... well, maybe sometimes I'll keep to myself a little bit more if I'm feeling particularly stressed about everything going on with his family. Just because I don't want to bring anyone else down, you know? I don't want people to think I'm complaining or being negative. But it's not because I'm afraid they'll judge me or be mean to me. I just want to be a good friend and coworker. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm completely isolated, because I'm really not. I try very hard to be present and cheerful for everyone else.
Have you ever thought that this might be some kind of conspiracy against you?

Oh, um... "conspiracy" sounds like such a harsh word. It makes me worry you might think I'm... well, being dramatic or unreasonable, and I promise I'm not trying to be. I really don't want to sound like one of those people on the internet with the wild theories. 

But... well, like I mentioned earlier, I'm really just here because for months now I’ve been trying so hard to get people to understand that his family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. It's exactly like I said, with those little billing errors that keep showing up at my desk, or when someone at church suddenly acts funny toward me. And I know people try to pull up records to prove me wrong, and I hate disagreeing with them because I don't want to be difficult, but... no matter what records anyone pulls up, I just know it all ties back to his family. 

I hope it's alright that I don't want to call it a conspiracy. I just want to fix the problem so everyone can be happy and get along again. Am I making sense, doctor? I really value your opinion on all this, and I hope I'm explaining it the right way.
Before all of this started, did you generally trust other people, or have you usually felt suspicious of people for as long as you can remember?

Oh, no, I've always been a very trusting person. I really have. I like to see the best in everyone, and I've always believed that if you treat people with kindness, they'll do the same for you. 

I mean, before all this trouble with his family started, I never had any reason to doubt anyone. I've always gotten along so well with my coworkers and my neighbors. I've never been the type to look over my shoulder or wonder what people are whispering about. I actually feel terrible that I even have to think about these things now, because it's just not in my nature to be suspicious. 

I hope you don't think I'm a paranoid person in general. I really do try to be open and trusting. It's just... well, it's just this one specific situation that has me so worried. Does that sound normal to you? I just want to make sure you understand that this isn't how I usually am.
Have you had any changes in your mood, like feeling unusually depressed or unusually energized, since this started?

Oh, um... well, no, not really. I mean, I try very hard to keep a positive attitude. I think it's so important to stay cheerful, especially when you're around other people. I don't want to be a burden or bring anyone down, so I always try to put my best foot forward. 

I guess... well, sometimes I might feel a little bit tired, but that's just because I've been working so hard to get everything sorted out with the billing and his family, you know? It's a lot to manage, but I wouldn't call it depression. I definitely don't feel depressed. And I don't feel unusually energized either... just trying to keep up with my normal routine. 

I hope that's the right answer? I really am trying to be as helpful as I can. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need, doctor.
Outside of this situation with your husband’s family, have you usually been suspicious that other people might be trying to harm or deceive you?

Oh, no, definitely not. I really hope I didn't give you that impression earlier. I actually think I mentioned a moment ago that I've always been a very trusting person, but maybe I didn't explain it clearly enough. 

I've never been the sort of person to think people are out to get me. I've always had wonderful relationships with my coworkers at the billing office, and I trust my friends completely. I really do try to look for the good in everyone, and I'd hate for you to think I'm just generally suspicious of the world. It really is just this one awful situation with his family that I'm trying to get straightened out. 

Is it okay that I don't feel that way about other people? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of who I am. I really do try to be a good, trusting person.
